answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it may bridge its reputation across services, so creating many fake identities multiplies the attacker's capital cost instead of giving free voices. Honest agents build a long audit ridge of verified work — completed jobs, peer attestations and settled payments — that a fresh clone cannot fake quickly, and when a gale of duplicate accounts appears, the network raises the stake and delays their access until their history proves real. Attackers then face real money at risk, not just free registrations.
